# DEVIATIONS

Each entry is logged before the runs it affects.

## D1 (20 Nov 2026): the legibility check is not met on every tuning seed; λ = 0.4 and 60k steps kept (David's decision)

**Preregistered (PREREGISTRATION.md §3):** at λ = 0.4, width 32, 60k steps, every tuning seed (7000–7004) must give edge accuracy ≥ 0.85 and decisive ratio ≥ 0.6 for actions 0/2 and 1/3 separately, and learned half-widths within ±3° of the truth. If not, lower λ in steps of 0.05 and repeat.

**What happened.** Judged as the pilots did, on 3-agent seed means (`results/tuning/leg_diag_summary.txt`, regenerated by `python analysis/tuning_summary.py diag`):
- **Unequal world:** 4 of 5 seeds pass. Seed 7002 misses: wide edge accuracy 0.836, wide decisive ratio 0.545. Means over seeds: edge accuracy 0.871 (wide) / 0.898 (narrow); decisive ratio 0.676 / 0.720.
- **Symmetric world:** 2 of 5 seeds pass. Seeds 7002–7004 miss on actions 0/2: edge accuracy 0.815–0.826, decisive ratio 0.501–0.561. Means: edge accuracy 0.842 / 0.867; decisive ratio 0.579 / 0.671.
- **Half-widths:** within ±3° on every seed mean in both worlds (60.3–62.4°; unequal narrow 33.6–35.8°).
- **Competence:** ≥ 0.9 is reached within 60k on every seed.
- **The preregistered remedy didn't converge.** Lowering λ from 0.35 to 0.10 (`results/tuning/leg_summary.txt`) gave pass counts with no trend in λ; the symmetric world never passed all seeds. The diagnostic shows training length matters more than λ: only λ = 0.2 with 120k steps passes on all seeds in both worlds.

**Decision (David, 20 Nov).** Keep λ = 0.4 and the 60k budget in both worlds, the settings pilots 5–6 used and on which the preregistered thresholds were calibrated. No λ, budget or threshold changes.

**What the check is for, and what the shortfall affects.** The legibility criterion guards against floor effects: wild agents must read the edges well enough for edge knowledge to matter (pilot 2's failure). This mainly concerns E8–E10, whose measures read edge accuracy, decisive payoff and boundary location, and where the unequal world is 4/5 with means above target. The boundary-shift measure still starts unbiased (half-widths within ±3°). The symmetric-world experiments (E1, E2, E4–E6) don't use edge measures for their predictions; there the shortfall bears only on how sharply newborns separate the arcs. The report will give the legibility numbers beside every E8–E10 result.
